sources.entry: llama-cpp-python - Python bindings for llama.cpp, for running GGUF models locally.

summary.one_liner: Python bindings for llama.cpp that let you run GGUF language models locally, with a low-level ctypes API, a high-level completion/chat API, and an OpenAI-compatible web server.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a ctypes binding to the llama.cpp C API, mirroring llama.h. On top of that it offers a high-level Llama class for text completion, chat completion, and embeddings, with OpenAI-style output formats. It supports JSON and JSON Schema response constraints, function/tool calling through chat formats such as functionary and chatml-function-calling, and multimodal (vision) models via several chat handlers. It also includes speculative decoding through prompt lookup, and can pull GGUF models from the Hugging Face Hub. An optional server module exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, and a Docker image is published on GHCR.
use_cases: run GGUF models locally from Python
drop-in OpenAI API replacement for local models
structured JSON output from a local LLM
vision and image question answering with local models
tool or function calling with open models
how_to_run: CMAKE_ARGS="-DGGML_CUDA=on" pip install llama-cpp-python  # optional CUDA build
stack: C/C++ compiler (gcc, clang, MSVC, MinGW, Xcode)
notable: Low-level ctypes binding that mirrors the llama.cpp C API, plus a high-level managed Llama class
OpenAI-compatible web server that can act as a drop-in replacement for the OpenAI API
Pre-built wheels available for CPU, CUDA, Metal, ROCm/HIP and Vulkan, alongside source builds
Multimodal chat handlers for LLaVA, Moondream, Qwen2.5-VL, Gemma 4 and other vision models
Speculative decoding via prompt lookup and JSON Schema-constrained generation
caveats: The README recommends building from source for hardware-optimized performance; pre-built wheels are described as basic or community-provided in places
Running on phones is only noted as possible via Docker on termux with root
Apple Silicon users must use an arm64 Python build or the x86 build will be much slower
